title: Transformations
objective: Stack copies of a rectangle into a twisting tower.
learn: Move and Rotate — and how a list of values transforms one object into many.

nodes.need: a list of heights, one per copy
nodes.hint: Sets › Sequence. Start 0, step = Spacing, count = Count.
nodes.correct: Series gives one value per floor: 0, 0.8, 1.6 … Those values will become both heights and twist angles.

wrong.range: Range divides a domain — you’d have to work out the total height first. Series lets you set the spacing directly.
wrong.slider: One slider = one number. We need one value per copy.
wrong.listItem: List Item picks from a list that doesn’t exist yet.
wrong.*: This slot needs a list of heights, one per copy.

nodes.need: vectors pointing up, one per height value
nodes.hint: Vector › Vector. Its factor F sets the length.
nodes.correct: Unit Z with a list of factors produces a list of upward vectors of increasing length — one motion per copy.

wrong.unitX: Unit X would push copies sideways, not up.
wrong.vector2pt: Vector 2Pt needs two points; we just have numbers.
wrong.constructPoint: Construct Point makes positions. Move needs motion vectors.
wrong.*: This slot needs vectors pointing up, one per height value.

nodes.need: a transform that shifts geometry along a vector
nodes.hint: Transform › Euclidean. G for geometry, T for motion.
nodes.correct: Move copies the geometry along each vector. One rectangle × a list of vectors = a stack of rectangles.

wrong.mirror: Mirror reflects across a plane — it can’t stack copies upward.
wrong.scale: Scale resizes; the rectangles would stay on the ground.
wrong.extrude: Extrude would make one solid wall, not separate floors.
wrong.*: This slot needs a transform that shifts geometry along a vector.

nodes.need: a transform that turns each copy by an angle
nodes.hint: Transform › Euclidean. Angle is in radians.
nodes.correct: Rotate turns each rectangle by its own angle (height × Twist). Higher floors turn more — a twisting tower from one rectangle.

wrong.mirror: Mirror flips geometry; it can’t twist gradually.
wrong.flipMatrix: Flip Matrix restructures data trees — it doesn’t touch geometry.
wrong.*: This slot needs a transform that turns each copy by an angle.

check.prompt: Which input of Move takes the Unit Z vectors?
check.correct: T is the translation (motion) vector. With a list of vectors, Move makes one copy per vector.

wrong.G: G is the geometry to move — the rectangle is already plugged in there.
